question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y+5z &=27 \\ y-5z &=-30 \\ z &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 5 & 27 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -30 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+5R_{3},\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 5 & 27 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}-5R_{3},\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -5 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+5R_{2},\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-3 \\ y &=0 \\ z &=6\end{aligned}\right..
$$

So, we have the solution $x=-3$, $y=0$, and $z=6$.
